Maya R: Quick canary heads-up — mixing prefill + decode into the same continuous batch on c-412 increased p95 by ~18% for the 8k token workload. Profiling points at kernel churn and KV cache thrash.
Tanya K: numbers + what did the queue look like? single combined queue?
Maya R: yes single queue, default continuous batching. Baseline (separate prefill-only before) p95=210ms; combined p95=248ms. Throughput slightly up but tail latency regressed.
Maya R: Flamegraph snippet (summary):
```
- prefill: long contiguous matmul kernels (optims used)
- transition: many small kernels + GEMM fallback (~0.8ms/token extra)
- decode: KV write/read hot paths thrash LRU, more mem copies
```
Julian: makes sense. Kernel switch penalty at the phase boundary can add a lot when you get many mixed short prefills followed by long decodes.
Aneesh: do we see more KV evictions or just extra read cost?
Maya R: both. Eviction rate up ~3x in the combined test; also more small-read syscalls at decode start. Looks like mixing sequence-length distributions causes bad cache residency.
Tanya K: strategy idea: split batch formation into phase-buckets (prefill bucket vs decode bucket), each with its own token_budget_target and max_batch_size. That way we avoid interleaving that forces kernel/kv context switches.
Maya R: I prototyped a queue_policy draft:
```
{
  "buckets": [
    {"phase": "prefill", "token_budget": 4096, "max_batch": 32, "priority": 10},
    {"phase": "decode",  "token_budget": 1024, "max_batch": 64, "priority": 5}
  ],
  "phase_transition_timeout_ms": 8,
  "allow_prefill_padding": true
}
```
Julian: Nice. Also consider "prefill-first windows" where we strictly drain prefill bucket for X ms before pulling decode. That amortizes kernel set-up cost.
Aneesh: add per-model kernel preference hints so runtime picks the high-throughput kernel for prefill if model supports padding to a multiple — can avoid small-gemm fallback when possible.
Sasha: I'll run an AB with three arms: (1) baseline combined, (2) bucketized as Maya's config, (3) bucketized + kernel-hints. Can push canary c-412->c-415 later today.
Maya R: thanks — also watching KV sizing. I raised KV cache high-water for the bucketized run to reduce evictions. Config tweak: `kv_cache_high_water=0.85` (was 0.7).
Tanya K: small thought — if decode has many short steps, we might prefer smaller token_budget but higher max_batch to allow many short decodes to coalesce. Keep the budget low to avoid starvation of prefill.
Maya R: agreed. That's why decode token_budget=1024 and max_batch=64 in draft.
Julian: for metrics, add per-phase p95 and kernel-switch count in the trace. Kernel-switch metric will tell us if padding + kernel-hints reduce churn.
Sasha: will add datadog widgets: prefill_p95, decode_p95, kernel_switch_count, kv_evictions. Tag by canary id.
Dev-Bot: deploy c-415 succeeded to eng-runtime-canary-2 at 2026-03-17T15:42:02Z :white_check_mark:
Aneesh: if AB shows improvement, next step is to propagate bucketization to dedicated runtime and add opt-in flag for Private packages.
Maya R: one caution — ensure phase detection is cheap (don't block per-request). Use request metadata (is_prefill boolean) or detect first token op; do not run expensive analysis in hot path.
Tanya K: good call. We'll pass a phase flag in the RPC: `phase: "prefill"|"decode"` — default fallback is combined queue.
Maya R: final ask — can someone run long-run stability with bucketization + high KV HW for 6 hours? I'm worried about memory blowup in tail. @Sasha? :thinking:
Sasha: got it. kicking off 6h run on c-416 and will post graphs + raw traces in this thread.
Maya R: perfect. If results look good we'll draft a changelog and rollout plan (canary -> staged -> GA).
Julian: also file a perf regression ticket linking these traces and the kernel hints PR so we have end-to-end traceability.
Aneesh: I'll add a unit test for the queue selector and a micro-benchmark to validate kernel hint effectiveness.
Maya R: thanks team. tagging this for follow-up in tomorrow perf sync.
